title: Students, opposition parties protest in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner
seoTitle: Delhi protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

tea.why: Protesters raised concerns about the functioning of the Election Commission and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
tea.want: They demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and action against him.
tea.changed: Oct 5: A Delhi court granted bail to 17 protesters accused of vandalism and defacement of public property during the demonstration.

summary: On October 2, students and opposition parties held a protest near Jantar Mantar in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Organised by groups including AAP, AISA, and RJD, the demonstration raised concerns about alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and demanded Kumar's resignation. Delhi Police denied permission for the gathering, imposed prohibitory orders, and deployed personnel, detaining nearly 1,000 protesters. The protests continued into October 4. Three female journalists later alleged sexual harassment by police officers during the events, prompting a police inquiry. On October 5, a Delhi court granted bail to 17 arrested protesters.

response: Delhi Police denied permission for the protest, imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, deployed thousands of police and paramilitary personnel, and used barricades. They detained nearly 1,000 protesters, including political leaders and activists. Police also launched an inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment…

crowd.text: Police sources said around 3,000 to 4,000 people were expected to attend the gathering.

injuries.text: One police officer has allegedly sustained injuries as per the MLC produced by the Investigating Officer

updates.text: Delhi Police denied permission for the protest and imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS in New Delhi district.
Several protesters and political leaders, including AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj and Atishi, were detained near Jantar Mantar.
Delhi Police detained nearly 1,000 people, including political leaders and activists, during the protest.
Three female journalists alleged sexual harassment by police officers during the protests.
Protests continued into Sunday in the capital, including by left-wing groups and CJP supporters.
Delhi Police forwarded the sexual harassment complaints to the crime branch for a detailed probe.
A Delhi court granted bail to 17 protesters accused of vandalism and defacement of public property.
